STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large relative to the food, so about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the food piece is roughly a rectangle about 4-5 cm wide. Across the plate's visible width (~7-8 food-widths... the plate spans roughly 2 food-lengths of the piece per 10 cm), the plate width comes out near 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm, square, area 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Single pizza-style slice (cheese and tomato sauce on a bread base), roughly 8 x 5 cm footprint = 40 cm² (about 6% of plate area).
- Thickness: a slice of pizza is about 1.5 cm, counted as one layer.
- Volume: 40 cm² x 1.5 cm = 60 ml.
- Grams: 60 ml x 1.0 (mixed cheese/sauce/bread, averaged toward bread's lower density) ≈ 60 g. Use 55 g as a reasonable estimate given the thin crust.

Hidden food: none visible beyond the slice; the stray crumbs are negligible.

STEP 4 - Total ≈ 55 g, a small portion on a large plate.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: pizza (cheese and tomato) is about 260-280 kcal/100 g. Use 270.
Energy ≈ 55 × 2.7 ≈ 150 kcal.
